clue.text: A spot of cards achieves nothing in bad night, breaking into much more than a sweat?

definitions.text: breaking into much more than a sweat?

parts.note: a pip is one of the spots printed on a playing card

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the jumbled letters of night
a bad night is a disordered one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A gambler's losing streak at cards leaves them sweating through a restless night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns NIGHT into INGHT, and 'in' puts O inside it after the G to give INGHOT. The definition describes the state of someone so overheated that sweating is an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scalding is far hotter than the warmth that merely makes a person perspire.

clue.text: Introduction green petrol doesn't have

definitions.meaning: an opening passage or preliminary that leads up to the main matter
unleaded fuel is sold as the environmentally friendly kind, having no lead put into it

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly motorist explains what their unleaded fuel leaves out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, lead in: that is what unleaded petrol lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening remark or preamble that brings a listener into a topic is a preface to it.

clue.text: Nudes are exciting, in the main

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Naked swimmers are thrilling to see out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic name for the open sea, so 'in the main' means below the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the ocean, so something located there lies beneath its surface.

clue.text: Country deposing its first queen

indicators.note: deposing means removing from the top position, so the leading letter of the country is shifted elsewhere

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A nation overthrows its first female monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The I at the head of IRAN is moved to the end, giving an Indian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is the wife of a rajah or a reigning Hindu princess, a royal consort in India.

clue.text: Sportsman won't see the point of this binding Monday's solution work — The Iliad?

indicators.note: binding means wrapping around, so the fencing sword encloses the word for work

parts.words: Sportsman won't see the point of this
parts.note: a fencer facing an épée will not see its tip coming, so the phrase describes that sword
op is the short form of opus, a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A fencer misses the joke in a Monday puzzle answer about Homer's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monday's solution' is the setter's aside that the fencing sword was an answer in that week's Monday puzzle; those words give no letters, and 'binding' wraps the sword round the work.
explanation.definitionFit: An epopee is an epic poem, and Homer's war story of Troy is the classic example.

clue.text: Physicist's in business after export from Java

indicators.note: the word for in business follows the Java program in the answer

parts.note: an applet is a small program written in the Java language and sent out to run in browsers
on means running or in operation, as a business that is open

explanation.surface: A scientist has a trading venture importing goods from Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: Java looks like the island, but here it is the programming language. Edward Appleton was the British physicist who discovered the ionosphere layer named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Appleton won the Nobel Prize for research into the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Inverted new party wear

indicators.note: inverted means the order of the two pieces is turned around from how the clue gives them

parts.note: a do is an informal party or celebration

explanation.surface: A fresh party, turned upside down, needs something to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists N then DO; 'Inverted' swaps the two pieces, giving DO then N.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, which is what wearing them begins with.

clue.text: Do take a bow!

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
a violin is played by drawing a bow across it, so it is the instrument that takes one

explanation.surface: A performer is told to step forward and acknowledge applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a bow!' reads as applause for a performer, but here it describes the violin, which a bow is drawn across.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone is to cheat them, and a violin is the stringed instrument played with a bow.

clue.text: Unfit one catching the spirit?

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite or spirit
a roper is someone who catches animals with a lasso

explanation.surface: Someone out of shape tries to trap a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse order to the clue: one who ropes an imp would be an imp-roper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable or not fitting for the occasion is described as wrong in that setting.

clue.text: 007's colleagues find a place of convenience …

parts.note: the Gents is a British name for a men's public toilet, a convenience

explanation.surface: Fellow spies are sent looking for a public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: James Bond, 007, is a secret agent, so his colleagues are spies. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is a secret service operative, so his fellow spies share his job.

clue.text: … to go to get intelligence — bird!

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate
wit means mental sharpness or cleverness

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the toilet clue, someone answers nature's call and wises up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' in the toilet sense continues the scene from the previous clue. The peewit is the lapwing, named for its call.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is another name for the lapwing, a crested plover of fields and moors.

clue.text: Devoutness exhibited by Ruth covering the tab

indicators.note: covering means surrounding, so the word for compassion goes around the drug

parts.note: ruth is an old word for compassion, as in ruthless
E stands for ecstasy, a drug sold as tablets

explanation.surface: Faith is shown by a woman called Ruth who picks up the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a woman's name, but it is the old word for pity. 'the tab' looks like a bar bill; here it is an ecstasy tablet, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being devout means showing reverence for God, which is religious dutifulness.

clue.text: Amongst the elite, Togo's Resort Hopper

indicators.note: amongst means in the middle of, so the jumbled letters go inside the word for the best

parts.note: the pick of a group is its best, its elite

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A West African holiday resort is full of the rich and famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort, the anagram signal; 'Amongst' sets the jumbled country name inside the word for the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a spring-loaded stick that someone stands on to bounce along.

clue.text: After business, new deal Capone hatched something dangerous found repeatedly here

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the business abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: a plot that is hatched is devised or contrived, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, plots a new deal after doing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hatched' signals the anagram of the three words naming the Chicago gangster's plan. 'found repeatedly here' points to the puzzle's theme of weapons hidden in its answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden gun or knife is a threat carried out of sight, such as a pistol in a pocket.

clue.text: Fulham fan's silver pin sticking out?

indicators.note: the pin is pictured protruding around the metal, so the word for pin surrounds the silver symbol

parts.note: a cotter is a pin or wedge used to fasten machine parts
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A football supporter wears a silver badge pinned prominently.
explanation.walkthrough: Fulham Football Club plays at Craven Cottage in London, so its fans are nicknamed Cottagers.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of Fulham Football Club are nicknamed after their stadium, Craven Cottage.

clue.text: Reach up and out, maybe, fry spawning

indicators.note: frying cooks something up, so these letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Young fish are hatching in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fry' looks like young fish, the subject of 'spawning', but it is the anagram signal. The definition pictures arms or wings stretched up and out.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance between the tips of the outstretched wings or arms is a measure of span.

clue.text: Your damn retrospective is reminiscent of Hollywood

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: yr is the short written form of your
rats is an exclamation of annoyance, like damn

explanation.surface: A grumpy film fan says looking back on your career recalls Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' reverses YRRATS as a whole to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood is famous for celebrities, so an atmosphere full of film stars recalls it.

clue.text: The generation gap closed collecting up refuse

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
closing the gap between the words lets a run of letters be gathered across them

explanation.surface: Young and old patch up their differences and gather up the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gap closed collecting' takes EGENER from thE GENERation, and 'up' reverses it. Refuse looks like rubbish, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or commitment is to decline to honour it.

clue.text: Snack one misguidedly selected to finish early

indicators.note: acting misguidedly is going the wrong way, so the two letters for one are switched

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping before the last letter of the word for selected

parts.note: chose means selected or picked

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly picked a snack and stopped eating before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguidedly' turns AN into NA, and 'to finish early' cuts the last E from CHOSE, giving CHOS.
explanation.definitionFit: These Mexican tortilla chips topped with cheese are a common bar food.

clue.text: Last sign of zodiac, then fifth, losing a little light

indicators.note: the final letter of the word zodiac is taken

parts.note: and means then, as in one thing and then another

indicators.note: losing a little means dropping a small part, the final letter, of the star sign

parts.note: Leo is the fifth sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An astrologer counts the signs of the zodiac by the glow of a candle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last sign of' looks like it means Pisces, the final sign, but it takes the last letter of zodiac, C. 'losing a little' cuts LEO to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a burning wick is a small source of illumination.

clue.text: With BA? DE lacking desire

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the two named letters are removed

parts.note: a BA is a university degree, so someone with one is degreed

explanation.surface: A graduate with a Bachelor of Arts is missing some qualification they wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes DE from the front of DEGREED, leaving the answer. The clue spells out the letters D and E it removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive wanting of money or food is avarice, an intense longing.

clue.text: Self-descriptive anagram caught the spirit

indicators.note: the word anagram describes the very operation it undergoes, so its own letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A word that names itself is captured along with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-descriptive' tells you to take the word anagram literally and rearrange it to ARMAGNA, then add C.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony in France, a distilled alcoholic drink.

clue.text: René's in, promoting clubs' source of apples in Calvados

indicators.note: promoting means moving up ahead, so the clubs and apple letters go before the French word

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: the first letter of apples is its source

parts.note: René is a French name, and the French word for in is en

explanation.surface: René joins in, moving clubs to the front, and finds the source of apples in a Normandy brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves C and A in front of EN. Calvados is both the Normandy apple brandy and the French department whose capital is Caen.
explanation.definitionFit: Caen is the chief city of the Calvados department of Normandy in France.

clue.text: What's normal for oomph and more oomph to ring in New Year?

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal, oomph

indicators.note: ring means surround, so the letters for the new year encircle the word for allure

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New Year
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: Partygoers wonder what counts as normal when ringing in the New Year with extra energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring in the New Year' looks like a celebration, but 'to ring in' is the container signal. Both pieces for oomph are crossword words for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind is the normal mental state, the opposite of madness.

clue.text: A record peak

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: An album reaches the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, especially one in Switzerland.

clue.text: Flier struggling with a gale in the diocese

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for the bishop's area

parts.note: a see is the area a bishop governs, a diocese

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot battles high winds over the bishop's district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' signals the anagram of the two words for the wind, and 'in' sets them inside the bishop's seat after its first letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed eagle is a large raptor that hunts along coasts.

clue.text: Swimmer's completely frozen?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the swimmer

parts.note: all means wholly or entirely
ice is frozen water, so frozen gives ice

explanation.surface: A cold-water bather is chilled to the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer here is a fish: the allice shad is a European herring-like fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The allice shad is a European fish of the herring family that runs up rivers to spawn.
